No amount bound in the TSS payment builder

findings.title: Sponsored invoke-host-function XDR signed with distribution account without contract/function/argument allowlist
Simulation auth entries and Soroban data from RPC applied without inspection before distribution-account signing
No cumulative spend limit in TSS
No amount bound in the TSS payment builder
TSS pays any destination in the queue row

failing_checks.title: Per-action amount bound
failing_checks.reason: The handler signs whatever amount the queue row holds. It has no maximum, and no positive-amount check is visible. Any cap would have to live in the upstream SDP code, which was not reviewed.

failing_checks.title: Cumulative budget
failing_checks.reason: No cumulative or daily budget exists in the submitter. It pays every queued row. The only limiter, tx_processing_limiter, throttles batch size and does not cap value.

failing_checks.title: Recipient binding
failing_checks.reason: The destination comes straight from the DB row. It is checked only for a valid G or C address format. It is not checked against an allowlist.

failing_checks.title: Asset identity and units
failing_checks.reason: Assets use code plus issuer. The amount is rounded to 6 decimals, although Stellar allows 7. A value such as 0.1234567 is silently paid as 0.123457. Rounding up overpays, and any amount below 0.0000005 becomes 0.000000, which is a zero-amount payment.

failing_checks.title: Externally supplied transactions
failing_checks.reason: Externally supplied XDR is only checked for host function type and auth address; contract, function and args are not inspected, and the op is sourced from the distribution account.

failing_checks.title: Controls outside the prompt
failing_checks.reason: TSS has no amount cap, cumulative budget or destination allowlist; it pays whatever is in the queue row. Controls are assumed to live upstream in the SDP.

failing_checks.title: Stated purpose versus behaviour
failing_checks.reason: The sponsored handler signs externally supplied invoke-host-function XDR with the distribution account as source. It only rejects auth from infrastructure accounts. It does not allowlist the contract, function or arguments.
